questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: Read 9 first: how many derangements of 9 objects are there? Give the exact answer, and state the conclusion.
questions.explanation: A derangement has no fixed points; !9=133496. The formula n! times the alternating sum of 1/k! gives this. Plain n! overcounts because it includes arrangements fixing some object.
questions.hint: A derangement fixes no element; use the inclusion-exclusion formula.

questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: With 8 and 2, how many ways partition 8 elements into 2 unlabeled blocks? Give the exact answer.
questions.explanation: S(8,2) = 127 counts partitions of n labeled elements into k nonempty unlabeled blocks. Using C(n,k) would ignore that leftover elements must also be assigned.
questions.hint: Use Stirling numbers of the second kind.

questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: How many items force two into one of 7 boxes?
questions.explanation: By the pigeonhole principle, placing 7+1 items into 7 boxes forces some box to hold at least two, so the threshold is 8. With only 7 items each box could hold one.
questions.hint: One more than the number of boxes forces a collision.
